Sarsha McGurk

The Fighter
Four Titles.
One Rising Star.

Sarsha McGurk is a 23-year-old professional boxer who trains and coaches out of Legacy Gym on the Central Coast — the current WBO Asia Pacific, WBC Asian Gold, UBF and New South Wales State Champion.

After time on the sidelines with an injury, she's back into full training and building again — but she returns a different fighter. With the WBO Asia Pacific and WBC Asian Gold belts, she now sits at genuine regional level.

At that level, in her weight division, her opponents and her opportunities come from across the Asia Pacific and beyond — not just at home. Her position in the sport has changed, and the year ahead is about making the most of it.

Already Training At World Level
Inside Her USA Camp

Earlier this year Sarsha spent almost a month in the United States, training from Los Angeles through to Las Vegas at gyms like Pound for Pound and Wild Card Boxing — working alongside world-class fighters and learning from some of the best coaches in the game.

Pictured here with Hall of Fame trainer Freddie Roach at Wild Card. This is the level Sarsha is now operating at — and the level she needs to keep getting back to.

The Opportunity

Ready To Take The Call

With these belts come real opportunities — training camps and fights around the Asia Pacific and in the USA, where she's already been invited back. Chances like these move fast, often on short notice. Sarsha has the discipline and the flexibility to say yes and get on a plane — what she needs is the backing to make it happen. Year-round sponsorship builds a fund that sits ready, so the moment the right opportunity comes, she can action it at the drop of a hat.

What Year-Round Support Covers
Where Your Support Goes

Sarsha campaigns in one of the lightest divisions in the sport, where the best opposition and sparring sit overseas rather than at home. That means real, ongoing costs: her boxing and strength training, an ongoing rehab and recovery program, gear, and the travel and camps that take her across the Asia Pacific and into the USA. Sponsorship keeps all of it moving, all year.
